# `pick-list` commands

## `pick-list cancel`

Cancel a list with a reason: it holds nothing any more, and units it staged and did not ship go back to their bins.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Additional resources | customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/pick-list.cancel` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow pick-list cancel P-1 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Order changed" --json`

## `pick-list create`

Make a pick list at one site: for each open order line, what it has to ship and the site can give it, less what other open lists hold, from the item's default bin, then other bins (no bin last), lots earliest-expiring first, in pick order (bin, item, order date). Name `orders` (one list can be a wave) or `ready: true` for every order that can ship; `complete_only` keeps orders that ship whole. What the site cannot give is a short line naming other sites. Moves nothing. Off unless company setting pick_and_pack_enabled is on (E_FEATURE_DISABLED). Example: {"site": "Warehouse", "ready": true}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Additional resources | customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/pick-list.create` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow pick-list create --site Warehouse --ready --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Morning wave" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "pick-list create", "input": {"site": "Warehouse", "ready": true}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `site` | `--site` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Site to pick at; default the default site. |
| `orders` | `--orders` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Sales orders to pick, by number or id; one list may cover several (a wave). Give this or ready. |
| `ready` | `--ready` | boolean | no | no | false | Every open sales order with something that can ship at the site now, oldest first. |
| `complete_only` | `--complete-only` | boolean | no | no | false | Only orders that can ship whole. |
| `limit` | `--limit` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | At most this many orders. |
| `picker` | `--picker` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Who picks it: a user or free text. |
| `date` | `--date` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Date of the list; default today. |
| `memo` | `--memo` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |

## `pick-list enter`

Confirm picks on an open list: 1-500 entries, each a `line` (position), an `item` (with `sales_order` when the list holds it for two orders) or a scanned `code`; `bin`, `lot`, `serial_number`, `quantity` (base units, default 1) and mode add or set. Entries append under their own idempotency key, so two pickers can pick one list at once. Picking past a line warns; a serial number the books hold elsewhere warns. With a staging bin at the site, picked units move there. Example: {"pick_list": "P-1", "entries": [{"code": "WIDGET", "bin": "A1"}]}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Additional resources | customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/pick-list.enter` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow pick-list enter P-1 --entries '[{"code": "4006381334020", "bin": "A2"}]' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Scanned" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "pick-list enter", "input": {"pick_list": "P-1", "entries": [{"code": "4006381334020", "bin": "A2"}]}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pick_list` | `PICK_LIST` | string | yes | no | — | Pick list number or id.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `entries[].line` | inside `--entries` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | The pick line, by position or line_id. |
| `entries[].item` | inside `--entries` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Or the item picked (name, id or barcode). |
| `entries[].sales_order` | inside `--entries` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | With item: the order, when the list holds the item for two orders. |
| `entries[].code` | inside `--entries` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Or a scanned code: an item barcode, or a serial-number or lot label. |
| `entries[].bin` | inside `--entries` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Bin the units came from; default the line's. |
| `entries[].lot` | inside `--entries` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Lot picked (lot-tracked items). |
| `entries[].serial_number` | inside `--entries` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Serial number of the unit picked. |
| `entries[].quantity` | inside `--entries` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | Base units; default 1. |
| `entries[].mode` | inside `--entries` JSON array | literal["add", "set"] | no | no | "add" | add (this many more) or set (the line now holds this many; 0 with serial_number puts that unit back). |
| `date` | `--date` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Date picked; default today. |

| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |

### Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_COMPANY_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one company matches; use the id or Organization/Company. |
| `E_COMPANY_NOT_FOUND` | No such company. |
| `E_CONFIG_INVALID` | The configuration file could not be read. |
| `E_CONTEXT_IN_INPUT` | Input contains a context field. |
| `E_DB_BUSY` | Another Bookflow command is running on this data root. |
| `E_FEATURE_DISABLED` | This feature is not enabled for the company. |
| `E_FS_UNKNOWN` | The filesystem type of the path could not be determined. |
| `E_GUARD_REFUSED` | Bookflow's own safety check in the database refused this write, so nothing was saved. This is a Bookflow bug, not a problem with your input or your disk: please report it with this error's details and request id. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |
| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |
| `E_MIGRATION_FAILED` | A schema migration failed; the database was backed up first and is unchanged. |
| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |
